paper: TradingGroup: A Multi-Agent Trading System with Self-Reflection and Data-Synthesis
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock implementation of TradingGroup's five-agent chain, delayed outcome reflection, adaptive style, and volatility hard-intercept; not the missing Qwen3-Trader policy, PEFT checkpoint, or five-ticker daily backtest.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: A five-agent chain covers news sentiment, financial reports, stock forecasting, style preference, and final trading decisions, with an attached risk module and data-synthesis pipeline.
News and report agents denoise complementary information; the forecasting agent integrates their outputs with technical features and reflects on successful and failed analogous cases.
A style agent reflects on recent performance to choose aggressive, balanced, or conservative execution, and a decision agent merges all upstream analyses with past profit/loss experience.
Dynamic risk management scales stop-loss and take-profit thresholds with recent volatility and applies a hard intercept when risk limits are exceeded.

The data-synthesis pipeline labels forecasting and decision records only after outcomes realize, using directional success, confidence, relative performance, and transaction-cost penalties for later reflection and post-training.

five_agent_roles.news_sentiment_agent: Equal-rank denoising of surprise, attention, and recent-trend proxies.
five_agent_roles.financial_report_agent: Equal-rank synthesis of value, profitability, cash-flow, strength, and distress proxies.
five_agent_roles.stock_forecasting_agent: Past-reliability-weighted fusion of sentiment, report, and technical agent scores.
five_agent_roles.style_preference_agent: Select aggressive, balanced, or conservative forecast transforms from the preceding 20 outcome-labelled months.
five_agent_roles.trading_decision_agent: Apply the selected style and its stock-level volatility hard-intercept to issue the final score.

reflection_and_risk_policy.style_selection: highest mean RankIC over the preceding 20 fully realized months with lexical tie-breaking
reflection_and_risk_policy.hard_intercept: set positive recommendations to zero when current cross-sectional risk percentile exceeds the selected style threshold
reflection_and_risk_policy.data_synthesis_label: monthly RankIC of each upstream or style score with the subsequently realized next-month excess return
reflection_and_risk_policy.score_refresh: monthly; reflection histories contain only formation months strictly before the current formation
reflection_and_risk_policy.common_portfolio_adapter: frozen value-weighted long-short deciles with all six cost and missing-return paths

preserved_elements: a stock-forecasting agent integrating technical and upstream information
self-reflection from labelled past successes and failures
a style-preference agent choosing among aggressive, balanced, and conservative behavior
a final trading-decision agent that merges upstream analysis and style
a hard intercept that can suppress otherwise positive actions
outcome labels created only after returns realize
a reusable data-synthesis history feeding future decisions
approximated_elements: JKP surprises and attention replace retrieved and re-ranked news
JKP financial quality and value replace filing RAG passages
cross-sectional trend and risk characteristics replace daily technical indicators
rolling RankIC reliability replaces LLM experience summaries and retrieved cases
deterministic style transforms replace natural-language style prompts and account-state reasoning
risk-percentile interception replaces position-level ATR stop-loss and take-profit execution
delayed score histories replace the unavailable 1,080 chain-of-thought trajectories and PEFT dataset
invented_elements: the 60-month forecasting reflection window and softmax temperature
the three exact risk penalties, safety bonus, and intercept percentiles
mean RankIC as the style-selection reward
